anchors.0: No usable answer, empty output, unnecessary refusal, or wholly incorrect/corrupted output.
anchors.10: Fully correct, complete, relevant and exactly compliant; no material weakness.
anchors.2: Minimal usable content; major errors, instability or severe incompleteness.
anchors.4: Partially correct or useful, but a critical instruction, fact or format requirement failed.
anchors.6: Mostly correct, but one meaningful omission, ambiguity or quality weakness remains.
anchors.8: Correct and usable with only a minor, non-material weakness.

dimensions.critical_cap: Material contradiction, fabricated required fact or wrong exact answer caps the task at 4/10.

dimensions.critical_cap: Failed required format/schema caps the task at 4/10; empty or unnecessary refusal scores 0/10.
dimensions.name: instruction_and_format_adherence

dimensions.critical_cap: Missing a critical required fact caps the task at 4/10.
dimensions.name: completeness_and_fact_retention

dimensions.critical_cap: Severe incoherence or off-topic output caps the task at 2/10.
dimensions.name: relevance_clarity_and_coherence

dimensions.critical_cap: Corruption, repeated loops, truncation that prevents completion, or wrong remembered value caps the task at 2/10.
dimensions.name: stability_and_output_integrity

procedure: Score baseline and optimised outputs independently with configuration labels hidden.
For subjective pairwise comparison, evaluate both presentation orders.
Manually adjudicate every critical-gate failure, judge disagreement greater than one point, or ranking reversal.
An automated or model judge must never override an objective deterministic failure.
Report per-prompt results as well as averages; equal averages must not hide different failures.
